artifacts.notes: The record supplies identity, date, material, overall dimensions, public-domain status, and five image URLs. Its collection note says the object was made in threaded sections and that a possible fourth section is lost. It supports one exemplar only.
artifacts.rights_basis: The Metropolitan Museum of Art marks object 471458 isPublicDomain true and releases its collection data under its Open Access policy.

artifacts.notes: The 1792 by 4685 pixel image was visually inspected. It shows the complete surviving crozier in frontal profile: a volute and decorated head, socket, long sectional shaft, and foot. The museum's square mounting plate is display hardware and must not be copied as part of the liturgical object.
artifacts.rights_basis: The Metropolitan Museum of Art marks object 471458 public domain and makes this image available through its Open Access collection record.

work.author: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
work.description: The Metropolitan Museum of Art's cataloged North Italian crozier, dated circa 1360–1400. It is a complete material-culture exemplar of a crook, socket, and sectional shaft, not a normative specification for every Roman pastoral staff.
